title: Velocity Checkpoint

selected_categories.reasoning: The implemented interaction is fundamentally a single-question answer-checking loop with instant right/wrong feedback.
The player must solve a simple motion-equation problem using provided values and submit the computed result.
The main active input is pressing a button to validate an answer, but there is no resource accumulation or repeated tapping economy, so this is only a weak surface match.
The game uses lane, checkpoint, and speedster language, but there is no actual lane-switching or runner movement system in code.
The audiovisual framing strongly suggests neon running aesthetics, though mechanically it remains a quiz/puzzle microgame.

uncertainty_notes: The top two matches are strong because the code only implements a fixed educational calculation prompt.
All runner-related categories are thematic rather than mechanical matches.
The category universe does not include an explicit 'educational microgame' label, so quiz and physics puzzle are the most grounded fits.
The fifth-place picks are weak by design because the game is too narrow to map cleanly onto many mechanic-heavy categories.
